instructions: Put the flour and 1/2 tsp of the salt in a large bowl. Add 4 tbsp of the olive oil and mix. Add about 3/4 cup of water a little at a time, stirring, until it comes together into a soft dough.
Knead the dough on the counter for 3 to 4 minutes, until smooth. Cover it with the bowl and let it rest while you make the filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F and brush an 11 inch round baking pan with a little olive oil.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tsp of the salt. Cut the stems out of the chard and slice the stems 1/4 inch thick. Boil the stems for 1 minute, add the leaves and boil for another minute, until they wilt.
Transfer the chard to a colander and rinse with cold water. Squeeze out as much water as you can, then chop it. That should be about 2 cups.
Thinly slice the scallions, mince the garlic and chop 2 tbsp of parsley.
Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the scallions and cook for 1 minute, until soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the chard and the remaining 1/2 tsp of salt. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until the pan is dry. Transfer to a bowl and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Grate the Parmesan, which should be about 3/4 cup. Stir the parsley, Parmesan and pepper into the cooled chard.
Cut the dough in two, with one piece a little bigger. Roll the bigger piece into a round about 13 inches wide and fit it into the pan, with the edge hanging over the rim.
Spread the filling over the dough. Roll out the other piece to about 11 inches and lay it over the top. Fold the bottom edge over the top edge and crimp to seal.
Prick the top all over with a fork and brush with the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil.
Bake for 30 minutes, until golden. Let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then cut into wedges.
Serve warm or at room temperature. It's good cold too. To pack it for lunch, keep the cooled pie covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and eat it cold, or warm it in a 350°F oven for 10 minutes.
method_notes: No erbazzone page had ratings. It leads with Memorie di Angelina for the olive oil dough (the oil version of her lard crust), the blanched and squeezed chard, and the plain chard, scallion, garlic and Parmesan filling. Cesarine and Giallo Zafferano confirm the filling and add a little more cheese. Most Reggio versions have pancetta or lard; here the pancetta is left out so the pie is vegetarian, and the dough uses olive oil. The dough rests while the filling is made, but the pie is not a 30 minute dish: it is a bake-ahead one that is good cold.
